note: What the flight recorder instruments, system by system (docs/design/FLIGHT_RECORDER_DESIGN.md section 2). Never read a row as broader than its scope text. A row is 'Fully instrumented' only when it names a test in game/tests/recorder_test.gd that exercises it (checked by that test); everything not listed as instrumented is not recorded. Updated by the stage that instruments a system.
as_of: stage D1 + D2 choke points + D3 systems (identity, life, employment, government, crime, player verbs, save and load), 2026-10-23; schema 2 (SIM-GATE-01: hourly village snapshots, combat chases, the closing snapshot), 2026-10-24; D5 judgment and D4 relations shared hours, gifts and harm (Expansion 20 batch R3), 2026-10-26; X20-FINAL phase 3 (production, consumption and unmet-need flows; contracts and credit; relations' help, talk, cooling, courting and proposals; memory forgotten, personality, grievances, history; daily summaries; multiplayer), 2026-10-27

rows.interaction: top-level priority chain of NPCBrain.decide: which branch took the decision, the guard values (hunger, health, hour, role, job) read, branches before it passed over, later ones 'not evaluated'
rows.note: Branch level only. Job routines inside a branch (_plan_job, _crafter, _guard, _bandit ...), recipe order, seller and buyer searches, the labour market and succession are not instrumented (D4). Choices weighed by judgment (JudgmentWeighting.choose) are recorded with their own scores in full: see 'Judgment-weighted decisions'. A branch before the winner is recorded as passed over: the chain does not say whether its guard was false or its planner returned no plan. Factors are the values read before the call; scores do not exist in a priority chain.

rows.interaction: every plan-step action run by World._run_plan (about 60 act kinds): kind, args summary, ok or failed, parent = the plan's decision
rows.note: Scope: actions executed from a villager's plan. The effects inside an action (items made, coins paid outside trade, relations, contracts) are recorded only where another row of this file says so; a failed action carries reason act_returned_false (the code gives no finer reason). Actions called directly by other code (fights, the player's verbs) are not plan steps and are not recorded.

rows.interaction: walk lost (no path, no level route), station wait given up
rows.note: The two interruption points named. The walk-lost event for 'no path' is recorded by the same code but no test reaches it (the village map's path search never returned empty in the probe); 'no level route' and the station give-up are exercised. Other places that clear a plan (fights, collapse, death) are not recorded.

rows.interaction: World.trade: accepted and refused sales with participants, coins and items before and after
rows.note: Every call to World.trade, villager and player. Coin or goods changes made by code that does not call trade are not recorded here (see the coin audit).

rows.interaction: World.transfer: gifts, pantry, deposits, accepted and refused, with item changes before and after
rows.note: Every call is an event. Owners are named only for villagers, the player, household pantries and the granary; chests, carts, stalls, loot and other stores appear as inv:?. Item changes made by Inventory.add/remove called directly (8 sites edit items directly, many callers add or remove) are not recorded.

rows.interaction: hourly balance audit: each purse, the manor treasury and World.total_coins against the recorded coin changes; any difference is an unattributed event and an alert
rows.note: REC-D4: detects, does not attribute. About 150 coin mutation sites outside World.trade (wages, rents, tax, pay, rewards, tills, deposits ...) are not instrumented; their changes appear as unattributed events once an hour per holder, naming the amount but not the site. Holders audited: villagers, the player, the manor treasury, the world total (tills, reserves, loot, the offerings fund and courier fees are inside the total only).

rows.interaction: hourly samples of hunger, health, cell, doing and coins of each living villager and the player
rows.note: Samples only (REC-D3); a threshold crossing (starving, arriving) is not recorded as an event yet. Never a substitute for an interaction record.

rows.interaction: work outputs, crafting, eating
rows.note: X20-FINAL: every production (made_, mined_, felled_, dug_, cut_, farm_harvest_, farm_made_), consumption (eaten_, used_, feed_eaten_, burned_, broke_, spoiled_, poached_lost_, wild_eaten_) and unmet-need counter (missed_meal_, station_busy_, starved_, skill_short_, keeper_no_*, field_unsown_no_seed, farm_plot_*, supports_failed, work_refused, assay_refused, proposals refused or declined, contracts lapsed or unsigned, credit defaulted) moved inside an open event is a state row on 'world' (prop kind:counter, the world counter before and after) under that event, so the actor, the action and the decision are known. Moves outside any event (hourly world processes) are only in the snapshot's stats_delta. Quantities moved between stores outside World.trade/transfer are still not item rows.

rows.interaction: births (child, mother, father, household), deaths with cause and the purse passing to the heir or the loot, ageing into a role (child to adult, adult to elder), partnerships (courting villagers and the player), guardianship placements and the clan fallback, the player character's death
rows.where: Life.birth, Life.sync_roles, World.kill, damage_player, Life._player_dawn, Life.partner_player, Relations (proposal accepted), Guardianship.move and join_clan
rows.note: Not recorded: the starting population's ages and partner links (founding state, not events), courting stages and gifts (relations), the player adopting a child (Guardianship.player_adopt), pregnancy and fertility checks that did not lead to a birth, the old-age mortality rolls that did not kill. A death records what the dead carried only as the purse and its recipient; goods inherited are not itemised.

rows.interaction: job changes (taken, lost, switched) with the job before and after and the reason, vacancies opened and filled with the vacancy count, the manor's hiring wage offers raised and eased
rows.note: Not recorded: who applied and why they were passed over (the job market, seek_work, apprentice choice scores), vacancies that close because the trade is back at strength, a newcomer's selection, stall lets, job-switch scoring. A job change is recorded after the fact with its reason text only.

rows.interaction: the daily reeve_day and pay_guards passes as events with the treasury and granary before and after; tax collected per payer, wages (sage, reeve, guards, manor hands), repair and public-works purchases, granary purchases, tool purchases and advances, relief purchases, mine supplies, each as paired coin state changes; layoffs; unpaid wages
rows.where: NPCBrain.reeve_day, pay_guards, manor_flow call sites, MineSupply.procure
rows.note: Not recorded: the tax-rate decision (TaxPolicy.step) as factors, relief selection (which household, why), manor_work reservations and refunds (coins set aside for a job move between the treasury and the job), rents and sales to the manor (Property), stall and till money passed to the manor, the manor buying wheat from a settlement, the reeve's succession choices. Any treasury change the pass makes outside the listed sites shows as the difference between the pass's summary row and the sum of its flows; the coin audit still flags it.

rows.interaction: the player's thefts as seen by the village (offender, victim, witnesses, crime count), a guard's confrontation with the fine and goods returned (coins and goods before and after), raise_alarm with the reports it causes, report_crime, a bandit's robbery of a villager
rows.where: World.witness, guard_confront, raise_alarm, report_crime, NPCBrain.fight (bandit robbery)
rows.note: Not recorded: pickpocketing attempts and their odds, fencing recognition detail beyond the sell verb, the Expansion 19 judgment of a crime, bandit raids on stalls, deliver_report (the chases that fights, alarms and reports start are recorded since schema 2: see Combat chases), the case record and the pursuit states (GP-CRIME-PURSUIT A1-A3: read from World.stats justice_* counters in the hourly snapshot, the economy run's samples and the gate's manhunt probe; the hue and cry and the bell are recorded as crime occurrences; a chase that loses sight ends with reason lost_sight, one taken in with taken). witness records the witnesses present, not those who failed to notice.

rows.interaction: one row an hour of village-wide aggregates (population by role, employment, hunger, health, idle and lost villagers, fighters and engaged guards, currency, treasury, household purses, food in store, births, deaths, ties, friendships, courting pairs, judgment facts, the player's crimes, the hour's counts of events, trades, coins traded, actions, failed actions, walk-lost, crimes, chases and alerts, the game's w.stats counters that changed, wall time and memory); the same values at the session's end in session.json final_snapshot
rows.note: Aggregates only, read without side effects (judgment facts counted directly: its counts() flushes gossip). The *_h columns count what the recorder saw in the hour, so they share the recorder's own limits (an uninstrumented coin site is not a trade). wall_ms and mem_bytes describe the machine and differ between runs.

rows.interaction: each chase of NPCBrain.fight: from the tick a fighter's target is new to the line of fight() that clears it, with that line's reason (blocked, out_of_range, near_bandit_camp, target_gone, robbed, target_slain, bandit_low_hp; since GP-CRIME-PURSUIT A1-A3: taken, a beaten offender taken in, an ok outcome; lost_sight, the hand-over to the search of the last-known place; case_closed), or cleared_elsewhere / retargeted; fighter, target (the player marked), start and end distance, game minutes and seconds, blows struck
rows.note: Which code set NPC.target (raise_alarm, deliver_report, a blow answered, a bandit's choice) is not named: the chase begins at the first fight() tick. A target cleared outside fight() (the player's death, a kill by another) is closed at the next hour, so its end time is that hour. Villager-against-villager fights are recorded as chases too (fighter 'villager').

rows.interaction: each shared hour of a pair (Relations.share: kind work, social or met), each gift (Relations.give: the item leaving the giver and reaching the receiver), each harm (Relations.harmed: the victim's tie and every kin or friend tie it lowered); every one an event on the pair's tie (tie:<a>:<b>) with regard, attraction and days known before and after
rows.note: Scope: these three channels only. Regard and attraction are floats, so their state rows carry no delta.

rows.interaction: help (Relations.helped), the player's talk and closeness (talked, player_tick), defending, daily cooling and courting at dawn, befriending, proposals and their answers
rows.note: X20-FINAL: help and talk (events on the tie with what moved), cooling (one row a dawn: ties, regard and attraction sums before and after; not per tie), a villager taking an interest (candidates, whether judgment chose), court asking and proposals (wrappers around the unchanged bodies: outcome, the answer's words, stage before and after; suitor marked :player for a player). The player's closeness ticks (player_tick) are not recorded.

rows.interaction: offer, counter, accept, decline, deliver, lapse, debt, repay, default
rows.note: X20-FINAL: object threads contract:<id> and debt:<id>: opened (coins set aside: buyer and contract coin rows), delivered (items of both sides), paid (from the reservation to the seller), ended (fulfilled, cancelled, lapsed, with why and the coins returned); debts extended (goods), repaid (coins), defaulted; barter (goods both ways). Offers not taken up and signings appear only at their end. Services' work steps are paid rows without goods.

rows.interaction: REC-DIAG: every coin move of a storefront, trade-counter, stall or shop session till (sale into it, necessity, owner's pay, top-up, commission, settlement, escheat) as a till event with both sides; ownership and tenancy changes of buildings, stalls, pens, plots and fields (World.set_owner, set_tenant); a built stall abandoned by a holder who is gone; each till's coins and owner once a day (economy_day)
rows.where: BusinessMoney.after_trade, _settle; Stalls.after_trade, settle, daily; World.set_owner, set_tenant; WorldRecorder._economy_day
rows.note: Not yet: wages and rents of the player's premises, construction sites and deliveries, the player's own shop till moves (Business.deposit, withdraw, collect); an ownership change in the first game hour of a session (World.setup gives every building its owner then).

rows.system: Farming, mining, manor work, chapel, feasts, quests
rows.interaction: their scripts
rows.where: farming.gd, mining scripts, manor_work.gd, chapel.gd, feast

rows.interaction: only the register transitions of people who move between the village and the settlements and the births registered in a settlement; the abstract daily phases and couriers are not recorded
rows.where: Identity.move (leave and return via Migration), Identity.register_member (settlement births)
rows.note: REC-DIAG: each move between the village and a settlement as a migration event with its reason, people, coins and goods (Migration._book); a member's death with its cause (hunger, old_age, no_household_left); once a day each settlement's population, households, hungry households, coins, treasury, food and deaths (settlement_day); X20-SETTLE-FOOD: each food purchase between settlements (settlement_food_purchase: buyer, seller, item, units, coins, due day; refused lines as refused), each shortfall the traders could not buy with its reason (settlement_food_unmet, failed) and each delivery (settlement_food_delivery: interrupted when no trader or no household was left to take it). Not recorded: the settlements' daily steps in detail, their other trade, tax and journals, couriers (D6).

rows.system: Judgment (Expansion 19): facts, beliefs, gossip, ledgers, trust
rows.interaction: every fact published (type, actors with shares, victims, beneficiaries, value, tags: a lie, its refutation), every belief taken in (source, teller, hops, confidence; object thread fact:<id>), every telling that passed something on with the beliefs it gave as children, every ledger post (judgment_good / judgment_bad of an actor for a fact, before and after) and every trust move (before and after)
rows.note: A meeting with nothing to tell writes no gossip row (the shared hour is the Relationships row). Not recorded: memory salience fading, forgetting, fact retirement at the horizon, ledger decay, personality drift, anger, bonds and resentment (below).

rows.interaction: every JudgmentWeighting.choose (all 13 integrated decision domains and the family profiles): the chooser, the profile, the key, the chosen option and the selection policy as a decision row; every candidate as an alternative (feasible with its utility, or infeasible with the live code's why); for each feasible candidate every factor value, every weighted contribution, the family-name colour and the stubborn penalties; forgo with its utility
rows.note: In full: no alternative or factor is sampled or dropped; at the storage cap the session stops, keeps everything and is marked incomplete (REC-D2). When the family name alone would have refused, only the repeated choice without it is recorded (tiebreak colour_blocked).

rows.interaction: every family-priority decision (meal, pay, work, danger): the person, household, kind, chosen option and utility, the rule's own values (tier, temperament, threat, dependants, price, the dependant paid for) as factor rows, linked part_of from its weighted choice (whose factors carry family_child_need, family_spouse_need, family_parent_need, self_floor ...)

rows.system: Judgment: memory and temperament over time
rows.interaction: salience fading and forgetting, facts retiring at the horizon, ledger decay, personality and wisdom drift, anger, bonds, resentment and family stories' pending state
rows.where: JudgmentStore._forget, make_history, tell_family_history; JudgmentPersonality._log; JudgmentBonds.on_belief; WorldRecorder daily judgment_day
rows.note: X20-FINAL: each memory forgotten (faded at dawn, or crowded out while learning: then a child of that belief), each personality change (channel, subject, severity, trait deltas), each grievance and betrayal, each history record made or told to a child; daily judgment_day (the store's stats moved, memories held). Fading per memory and ledger decay (lazy, applied on read) are not rows: their effect is in the forgotten events and in the values every choice records.

rows.system: Judgment: NPC aspirations (Expansion 20 R5, WDR-011-C; off by default)
rows.interaction: every change of a villager's aspirations as event judgment/aspiration: a priority shift (success, setback, the loss of a partner, child or parent, marriage; with how the person met a setback: persevered, adapted, gave_up), a change of the leading aspiration, and the survival level crossing a step of aspiration.surv_record_step; in every JudgmentWeighting.choose with the layer on, the aspiration factor's domain, pressure, fit and survival level, the priority multiplier of each scaled weight (job_choice skill and growth, the courting factors) and the forgo row's aspiration offset
rows.note: Only while aspiration.enabled is on (shipped off). Not recorded: the daily satisfaction of each domain when no band, lead or survival step changes (it is saved in the judgment section's aspire rows). game/tests/aspiration_test.gd checks the event and the trace extras.

rows.interaction: the player verbs that change the world: trade (buy, sell), take, strike, craft, loot, each a verb event on the player's permanent reference with the pack, the purse and the target's health before and after; what a verb triggers (a trade, a witness, an alarm, a death) is its child
rows.where: World.player_buy_many, player_sell, player_take, player_craft, player_hit_npc, player_loot (wrappers); World.trade
rows.note: Not recorded: moving, eating, resting, equipping, dropping, harvesting, mining, felling, planting, building, renting, quests, spells (player_cast_fireball), player_home_move, pickpocket, lock picking, barber visits, the player's skill gains. The verb's state rows are a summary (authority summary): what a child event recorded is not counted twice.

rows.interaction: every register transition of a person with their permanent id: registered (founding, birth, newcomer, outlaw, arrival, settlement birth, player), left the village, returned (same id), died, became ancestor, became player; and succession as one event: predecessor and heir as two different references, the player role passing between them, the live -2 view's tie count before and after
rows.note: Scope: the register and the succession event. Events are recorded where the transition is made (Identity.*), so any code that changes a person's whereabouts without calling Identity.move is not seen. The founding population is recorded as registered_founding events at world creation.

rows.interaction: a loaded world: a session note with the save version, the count of people and whether their ids are unchanged (alert identity.ids_changed_on_load otherwise); a save written: a session event with the save version and register counters
rows.note: The load note is exercised by a test (mid-journey save, load, return under the same reference). The save event is called from main.gd save_game, which no headless test runs: the recorder method is tested directly. A game loaded with the recorder enabled attaches a new session; a loaded game never continues an earlier session's archive.

rows.interaction: once a game day: deposits left and worked out by ore, trees, households, regional coins and goods, capability levels and their changes, open contracts and reserved coins, open debts; the judgment store's stats moved; the LE-01 model's record counts and integrity (unbacked reservations raise a violation alert)
rows.note: Read only: plain fields and pure functions (judgment.stats, never counts(), which flushes gossip).

rows.interaction: host started, guest joined, refused, left; host lost (guest); each request the host applied with its result; a prediction the host answered differently; syncs counted; one net_state digest a game hour per participant (players, peers, a hash per shared section)
rows.note: A guest's world never simulates, so its archive holds only its network events and digests (no audit there). MML_RECORD=DIR records every process of the network harness. Moves and the per-tick villager and animal snapshots are not rows. tools/recorder_archive.py --participants compares the digests.
